CZI From Institutional Transformation to Industrial Transformation 2023-2027

description.narrative: Confederation of Zimbabwe Industries (CZI) "From Institutional Transformation to Industrial Transformation" är ett 3-årigt stöd på 25 miljoner kronor till CZI:s strategi som löper från 2024 till 2028 och som syftar till att stärka dess roll inom policy-forskning och påverkansarbete för ett gynnsamt företagsklimat i Zimbabwe. Genom sitt arbete fungerar CZI kontinuerligt som en viktig mellanhand mellan den offentliga och den privata sektorn. CZI formulerar evidensbaserade policy-förslag, engagerar regeringen i en substantiell och konstruktiv dialog och främjar handel inom och utanför Zimbabwes gränser. Dessutom kommer CZI:s arbete att leda till att företagsutveckling främjas med skapande av arbetstillfällen och entreprenörskap från undersektorn för små och medelstora företag och till minskad import i takt med att affärsförbindelser skapas mellan stora tillverkningsföretag och små och medelstora företag.

Confederation of Zimbabwe Industries (CZI)” From Institutional Transformation to Industrial Transformation” is a 3-year strategy support of SEK 25 million to CZI’s strategy running from 2024 to 2028 seeking to strengthen its role in policy research and advocacy of enabling business environment in Zimbabwe. Through its work, CZI continuously works as key intermediary between the public and private sector. It formulates evidence-based policy proposals, engage government in substantive and constructive dialogue and promotion of trade within and beyond Zimbabwe boarders. Furthermore, CZI’s work will result in promotion of enterprise development with job creation and entrepreneurship from the SMEs subsector and reduced imports as business linkages are forged between large manufacturing and small and medium enterprises (SMEs).

Goal Growth and Expansion of inclusive and sustainable economic activities
Objectives To create systemic pro-poor change in the business environment reform system, this project will work to: 1. Curate entrepreneurship opportunities and corresponding conducive environment 2. Create financing opportunities for off-taker backed green field projects 3. Advance Green Manufacturing, Sustainability and Climate Change modelling and phasing for start ups 4. Create a conducive business environment for manufacturing The intervention should result in the strengthening of confederation of Zimbabwe Industries (CZI) in its role and in creating sustainable, systemic change in the business environment.

Introduction
The Confederation of Zimbabwe Industries (CZI) received core funding to implement its 5-year strategic plan aimed at repositioning the organization for greater relevance, legitimacy, credibility, influence, and leadership. A good foundation has been laid in aligning CZI more closely with its mandate, responding to member needs, and adapting to emerging advocacy issues affecting businesses. Key achievements include contributions to policy development, strategic alliances, economic research and analysis, advocacy, and direct support to members. The reuslts will be for reporting period January to December 2024.
Key Results Achieved
1. Curate entrepreneurship opportunities and corresponding conducive environment
-CZI took a dual approach advancing Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) entrepreneurship, firstly by identifying new manufacturing opportunities and ecosystems gaps through research and secondly, directly supporting existing SME with visibility, standards and advancing entry and growth pathways.
CZI research revealed opportunities suitable for SMEs with scope for small scale manufacturing, supported by import substitution data and evidence of local demand in value chains like dairy, leather, cotton and sugar. It further developed scoring tools to rank value chains based on relevance and economic potential and these will be further supported with feasibility studies to inform support and enterprise development. This should result in SMEs being able to develop bankable proposals and seeking partnerships with established firms to engage in manufacturing businesses.
-CZI also focused on strengthening the ecosystem for existing SMEs by addressing barriers identified in the 2023 survey such as market exposure, financial constraints and meeting quality standards. CZI engaged Invest India for collaboration in adopting an industrial start-up kit which has helped SMEs in India to structure their initiatives. SMEs were further assisted with exhibition space at the SADC industrialization week enhancing their export market readiness, and through in-house exhibitions which provided buyer interaction opportunities. These opportunities will be followed through and reported in the next report. In partnership with Standards Association of Zimbabwe, a workshop was organized for SMEs to familiarize them with role of standards in scaling up and export markets.
-Further, CZI identified major structural constraints through the Manufacturing Sector Survey Report (MSSR) affecting SMEs, e.g. low-capacity utilization and high production costs; challenges which reduce competitiveness and stall growth for intermediate input manufacturing. With these insights, CZI engaged government to advocate for regulatory reforms, investment incentives, and reduce compliance burdens, this is expected to create a more predictable, growth-oriented policy environment for small manufacturers.
-CZIs studies such as those focused on industrial and economic research has gained reach and is being referenced by players in the economy and this expands the propagation of policy opinions across the economy. Organizations citing CZI work included World Bank, ILO, U.S Department of State Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe and Ministry of Finance, Economic Development and Investment promotion.
Source: CZI annual report 2024
2. Create a conducive business environment for manufacturing
CZIs work on creating an enabling environment for its members is done through various means which include engagements in the policy and business ecosystem, propagating policy opinion through research, advancing manufacturing interest through board representation, member accompaniment, policy papers and standing committees.
-Member accompaniment- CZI supported members for accompaniment and preparation of advocacy cases for engagement with policy makers through data analysis to support member submissions and facilitating engagements with policy makers. Advocacy cases with member accompaniment included trade, levies, utilities and prices and a total of 8 cases were resolved in sectors such as beverages, rubber and plastics, machinery and equipment and textiles, improving the ease of doing businesses for these sectors.
- CZI made a formal submission to ZIMRA (tax authority) as part of its member accompaniment process with issues focusing on automation of tax processes, addressing compliance inefficiency and refining communication protocols. The result was the synchronization of compliance between ZIMRA and Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe (RBZ) on imports and refining legislation impacting business operations. This reiterates CZIs role in creating a more efficient, business-friendly regulatory environment.
-Engagements in the policy and business ecosystem- Macroeconomic stability is a priority area for business as it provides a basic pillar on which to build competitiveness. Thus, CZIs involvement as part of boards and working groups such as Zimbabwe Arrears Clearance and Debt Resolution Process-Economic Growth and Stability working Group, allows them to continue advancing the interests of businesses, such as maintaining exchange rate stabilization and controlled fiscal deficit. The exchange rate has remained stable for the first half of 2025 and the government recorded a budget surplus in the budget mid-term review for 2025 although with domestic arrears.
-CZI advocated for the need of a transitional plan- Zimbabwe industrial reconstruction and growth plan (ZIRGP) 2024-2025 ensuring the country has adequate time and sets a good foundation for the next industrial plan and this was adopted. Further, the Ministry of Industry and Commerce adopted CZIs proposal to include the manufacturing for manufacturing pillar in the ZIRGP and ease of doing business, and competitiveness through review of the regulatory burden on businesses.
-CZI proposals were incorporated into the 2025 national budget prior to budget announcement and after through amendments, such as review of sugar tax and route to market measures, positioning CZI as a recognized platform for business advocacy.
-CZIs manufacturing sector survey report has become a key input into the policy ecosystems because it assesses policy efficacy and proposes policy measures needed to drive manufacturing growth. CZI was invited to partner with ZIMRA to build capacity of the industry to meet the AfCFTA standards, improving their preparedness and compliance and ability to seize opportunities within the continental market.
3. Create financing opportunities for off-taker backed green field projects
CZI identified emerging manufacturers with strong industrial promise which could be linked to manufacturing gaps in value chains such as glucose, cellulose and gang nails which are currently being imported. The SMEs were offered free membership connecting them to networks to foster exposure to established firms and gain access to knowledge and training. They were supported in their readiness for trade and investments with programmes like AfCFTA Protocol on Women in Trade provided practical insight into how entrepreneurs can become investment and trade ready. Moreover, conversations were initiated with value chain anchors to assess their interest in partnering with SMEs. This laid a foundation for operationalizing financing partnerships and scaling SMEs support into 2025 and beyond.
4. Advance Green Manufacturing-Sustainability and Climate Change modelling and phasing for start ups
-CZI focused on building a pipeline of future manufacturers and developing a roadmap to help start-ups phase sustainability. Studies done by CZI highlighted gaps in awareness, access to finance and strategic planning for low emission business models. An analysis by CZI helped it to put together a package for supporting start-up manufacturers to gradually integrate sustainability and compliance into their operations, in alignment with international expectations. This is a good foundation for future discussions and modelling of sustainability integration of climate smart practices, regulatory environment trainings and technical accompaniment planned for 2025.
-CZI managed to integrate gender into the sustainability agenda through its women in industry programme (WIN), where several initiatives were taken. CZI aims to ensure that green transition is both inclusive and economically transformative. Initiatives such as WIN masterclass profiling female leadership in packaging sector and skills in heels campaign spotlighting women participation in industry were done to embed gender equity into the sustainability conversation and promote procurement from women-owned businesses.
Lessons Learned and Adaptations
CZI recognized that each value chain presents uniqueand sometimes politically sensitivechallenges. This necessitated:
-Trust-building and politically informed approaches.
-Adjusted timelines to allow for deeper consultation and dialogue.
-Sector-specific strategies to enable tailored interventions and foster collaboration.
-Validation workshops with key stakeholders to promote constructive dialogue, consensus building, and refinement of proposed interventions.
Conclusion
The organizations ability to adapt to sector-specific challenges, build strategic alliances, and support members through data-driven engagement reflects a maturing institution committed to inclusive and sustainable industrialization. As CZI continues to refine its strategies and deepen stakeholder collaboration, it is well-positioned to drive meaningful change and support Zimbabwes journey toward industrial transformation.
